A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SynFlow, with readable corresponding methods, equations, seven tables and four figures. Both end with references; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original zero-shot evaluations, fine-tuning experiments, scaling studies and ablations on nuScenes, TruckScenes and Aeva.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Tables 2–7 and Figure 3.

M1.justification: The three data-generation policies, rigid-body flow-label construction, DeltaFlow backbone, losses and synthetic pre-training/fine-tuning procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same SynFlow training coverage and nuScenes, TruckScenes and Aeva evaluations, including the same real-data sources in the UniFlow comparison. Newly cited datasets are not newly evaluated.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain EgoMotionFlow, SeFlow, VoteFlow, SeFlow++, TeFlow, DeFlow, Flow4D, DeltaFlow and UniFlow. MambaFlow is newly cited but does not appear as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The synthetic splits, real-label budgets, 67-sequence Aeva evaluation, model configuration, optimization settings and evaluation metrics are unchanged. No added experiment or revised protocol is documented.

E4.justification: Both retain synthetic-data scaling, label-budget scaling, synthetic/real complementarity, generation-policy ablations and backbone comparisons in Section 6.2. The qualitative examples also remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed variability, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bars. The reported means remain metric aggregates rather than newly introduced uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 5 corrects the indicated OTHER-category winner: bold highlighting moves from the combined model's 0.401 to UniFlow-only's 0.359. This is a ranking-annotation correction; all numerical table entries and plotted scaling curves remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The scene-flow definition, temporal mapping, instance-tag assignment and rigid-body derivation in Equations 1–3 are unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: Both retain the motion-oriented pipeline novelty claim, SynFlow-4k contribution, zero-shot transfer, label efficiency and synthetic/real complementarity claims. Softer wording such as 'comparable to' instead of 'rivaling' does not materially redefine their scope.

C2.justification: Section 6.2 removes the explanation linking the pedestrian-error plateau near 0.47 to difficulty representing non-rigid motion through rigid-body simulation. It also revises the sensor-realism examples in the complementarity discussion. Section 6.4 retains the open-loop synthesis and domain-extension discussion.

D1.justification: The introduction replaces the GitHub pipeline/dataset pointer with a Hugging Face dataset pointer. Section 5.1 retains the hardware and 3–6-minute generation time but replaces the beam-specific qualification, including 64-beam being slower, with a general dependence on scene configuration.

R1.justification: v2 adds eight cited works: Zenseact, ONCE, Waymo, MambaFlow, VGGT-Omega, MotionSC, PointWorld and MolmoMotion. These broaden contextual references without substantially changing the paper's motion-oriented research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the opening introduction paragraph, streamlines the abstract and scattered explanatory passages, moderates rhetorical wording and corrects author/affiliation text. The section sequence and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 increases spacing, restyles paragraph headings and relocates Figures 3–4 and Tables 4–7 through text reflow. Figure content and table structures remain intact; Figure 2's caption is shortened and Table 5's best-result highlighting is corrected.

improvement.justification: v2 offers modest readability improvements and corrects Table 5's misleading winner highlighting, while adding contextual citations and a direct dataset pointer. However, it removes the explicit non-rigid pedestrian-motion qualification and makes generation-time information less specific. With the scientific evidence unchanged, these usability gains and losses in explanatory transparency do not establish a reliable net quality direction.
